I think this is the first time on Lavari that it genuinely felt like all four of them just wanted the episode to end. They looked completely out of ideas and seemed embarrassed, which is probably why they had to rely on audience questions. They even merged two different videos just to make the episode long enough. That says a lot.
And when Deep asked about the award, Abhishek's response—"tane nai samjay"—came across as pure arrogance. Deep may have already known about those awards; he likely asked because the audience would want to know. But Abhishek's reply indirectly implied that the audience wouldn't understand. That wasn't witty or clever—it just sounded condescending.

Then he said, "Kon star che?" Seriously? You're working in the Gujarati film industry, and if you don't value or respect the actors in your own industry, then you don't deserve to work alongside them.

This wasn't a case of someone being nervous and saying the wrong thing. If you compare this video with the later-part video that was actually shot earlier, you'll notice the exact same attitude. It feels consistent, not accidental.

I genuinely hope they don't invite him back on the show again.

Guys, one small feedback from a viewer who genuinely enjoys the show and has even attended a live Lavari episode. First of all, thank you for all the fun and entertainment, you guys are naturally hilarious and the chemistry between all of you is amazing.

But honestly, I would really like if guests were allowed to speak more during the episodes. Even in this episode, there were a lot of interruptions, and if you look at the comment section, many viewers seem to feel the same way. I understand the original live recordings are much longer, but while editing, it would be great if more meaningful conversations from the guests could be included.

For example, in the Devaki episode, it felt like she hardly got enough time to properly share her thoughts. On the other hand, Dharmesh sir’s episode was one of the best because he was given enough space to speak, and that made the episode feel more engaging and memorable.

You guys do not need to constantly prove how funny or entertaining you are, everyone already knows that and loves you for it. Your punches and reactions are great, but the guest should ideally have the highest talking time in their own episode.

No offense at all, just genuine feedback from someone who truly enjoys watching Lavari and wants the conversations to feel even better. Keep doing amazing work.

*"Gluten-free Jowar Chocolate Appe Cake (also known as Choco Balls)"* This is a healthy and perfect snack for kids' tiffins. It’s prepared in an appe pan (aebleskiver pan) in just 10 minutes without an oven or air fryer. *_Ingredients:-_* * Jowar Flour (Sorghum): 1 cup (Can substitute with Ragi or Bajra flour) * Powdered Sugar or Jaggery Powder: ½ cup * Cocoa Powder: ¼ cup * Milk Powder: ¼ cup (Adds richness) * Baking Powder: 1 tsp * Baking Soda: ½ tsp * Vanilla Essence: A few drops * Ghee or Oil: 2 tbsp * Milk: 1 cup (Room temperature) * Additional Ghee/Oil: For greasing and flipping *_Instructions:-_* *1. Prepare the Batter* * In a large mixing bowl, combine the jowar flour, powdered sugar (or jaggery), cocoa powder, milk powder, baking powder, and baking soda. * Add the vanilla essence and 2 tablespoons of ghee (or oil). Mix these ingredients well. * Gradually pour in the milk. Use about half first, then the rest, whisking until you achieve a smooth, thick batter. *2. Preheat and Grease* * Place an appe pan on the stove over low heat. * Lightly grease each mold with a little bit of ghee or oil. *3. Cook the Choco Balls* * Give the batter a quick stir. Fill each mold only halfway with the batter. Do not overfill, as the cakes will rise and double in size. * Cover the pan with a lid and cook on low flame for about 4 minutes. * Once the tops look set and the balls have puffed up, apply a tiny amount of ghee on top of each ball. *4. Flip and Finish* * Using a wooden stick or a small spoon, carefully flip each ball over. * Cook the other side for another 3 minutes on low flame. Do not cover the pan during this second stage to prevent steam from making the cakes soggy. *5. Serving* * Once cooked through, remove the choco balls from the pan. * *Serve* them warm or at room temperature. They pair perfectly with chocolate sauce, Nutella, or can be enjoyed plain as a healthy treat.

"Hara Chana Masala Recipe" (Green Chickpea Curry) Ingredients:- Main Ingredients: * Fresh Green Chickpeas (Hara Chana): 2 cups (peeled and washed) * Cooking Oil: 4 tablespoons * Onion: ½ cup (finely chopped) * Fresh Coriander Leaves: A handful (finely chopped for garnish) * Water: 3 cups (or 1.5 glasses) For the Fresh Paste: * Tomatoes: 2 medium (chopped) * Ginger: 2-inch piece * Garlic: 10 to 12 cloves Whole Spices (Tadka): * Cumin Seeds (Jeera): 1 teaspoon * Bay Leaves (Tejpatta): 1 to 2 * Cinnamon Stick: 2-inch piece * Black Cardamom (Badi Elaichi): 1 (crushed) Ground Spices: * Turmeric Powder: ½ teaspoon * Kashmiri Red Chili Powder: 2 teaspoons * Coriander Powder: 1 teaspoon * Cumin Powder: ½ teaspoon * Garam Masala Powder: ½ teaspoon * Black Pepper Powder: ⅓ teaspoon * Salt: To taste Instructions:- 1. Prepare the Masala Paste: Place the chopped tomatoes, ginger, and garlic into a grinding jar. Blend into a smooth, fine paste without adding extra water. Set aside. 2. Sauté the Aromatics: Heat 4 tablespoons of oil in a pressure cooker over medium heat. Once hot, add the cumin seeds, bay leaves, cinnamon stick, and crushed black cardamom. Add the finely chopped onions and sauté until they turn golden brown. 3. Cook the Tomato Base: Add the freshly ground tomato-ginger-garlic paste to the onions. Stir well and cook for about 2 minutes. 4. Add Spices: Lower the heat and add the turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, garam masala, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly and let the spices cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the oil starts to separate from the masala. You can add a splash of water (use the remains from the grinding jar) to prevent the spices from burning. 5. Sauté the Chickpeas: Add the 2 cups of fresh green chickpeas and salt to the cooker. Stir to coat the chickpeas in the masala and sauté for another 2 minutes. This allows the chickpeas to absorb the flavors. 6. Pressure Cook: Pour in 3 cups of water (adjust based on your preferred curry consistency). Close the lid of the pressure cooker. Cook on medium flame for 5 whistles. 7. "Masoor Dal (Red Lentil) Dosa Recipe" Ingredients:- For the Dosa Batter: * Masoor Dal (Red Lentils): 1 cup * Green Chilies: 2–3 (adjust to taste) * Garlic Cloves: 3–4 * Salt: To taste (approx. 1/2 tsp for grinding + 1/2 tsp for adjusting later) * Water: 1/2 cup (plus more if needed for consistency) * Cooking Oil: For frying For the Toppings (Optional): * Onion: 1 medium, finely chopped * Tomato: 1 small, finely chopped * Fresh Coriander: A handful, chopped * Peri-Peri Masala or Podi Masala: To sprinkle For the Green Chutney: * Fresh Coriander Leaves: 1 bunch * Garlic Cloves: 2–3 * Green Chilies: 2 * Lemon Juice: 1 tsp * Roasted Chana Dal (Dalia) or Sev: 1–2 tbsp (for thickness) * Salt: To taste * Water: As needed Preparation Steps:- 1. Prepare the Batter: * Wash 1 cup of Masoor Dal thoroughly. * Soak the dal in room temperature water for exactly 15 minutes. Note: Do not soak for longer, as the dal will become too soft and the dosa won't be crispy. * Drain the water and wash the dal 4–5 times under running water. * Transfer the soaked dal to a grinding jar. Add green chilies, garlic, salt, and 1/2 cup water. * Grind into a completely smooth paste. If the batter is too thick, add a little more water until it reaches a pouring consistency. * Transfer to a bowl and add another 1/2 tsp of salt (adjust to taste). Mix well. 2. Prepare the Green Chutney: * In a blender, combine coriander leaves, garlic, green chilies, lemon juice, roasted chana dal (or sev), and salt. * Add a splash of water and blend until smooth. Set aside. 3. Cook the Dosa: * Heat a non-stick tawa (griddle) over low-medium heat. * Lightly grease the tawa with a drop of oil and then wipe it off completely with a tissue paper. The surface should not be greasy. * Pour a ladleful of batter into the center of the tawa. Using the back of the spoon, spread it in a circular motion moving outwards. * For Veggie Dosa: Sprinkle chopped onions, tomatoes, coriander, and peri-peri masala on top while the batter is still slightly wet. * Drizzle a little oil around the edges and on top. * Cook on low-medium heat for about 3 minutes. Be patient; Masoor dal takes a bit longer to crisp up than rice dosa. * Flip (Optional): If you prefer it cooked on both sides like an Uttapam, flip and cook for 30 seconds. For a classic crispy dosa, cook on one side only until the base is golden brown and firm. 4. Serving: * Fold the dosa and serve hot with the prepared green chutney. 👍

Spicy Matar (Green Peas) Sandwich Recipe ​Ingredients:- ​For the Pea Filling: ​Fresh Green Peas: 1 cup (Fresh is preferred over frozen for better texture and flavor) ​Garlic: 3–4 cloves ​Green Chilies: 2 (adjust to spice preference) ​Oil: 1 teaspoon ​Salt: To taste ​For the Spicy Green Chutney: ​Fresh Coriander Leaves: 1 bunch ​Garlic: 2–3 cloves ​Green Chilies: 1–2 ​Lemon Juice: 1 tablespoon ​Roasted Chana Dal (Dalia): 1 tablespoon (or Sev Bhujia for thickness) ​Salt: To taste ​Water: A splash for grinding ​For Assembly: ​Bread Slices: 4 slices (White, Brown, or Sourdough) ​Cheese Slices: 2 slices ​Butter: For toasting ​Instructions:- ​1. Prepare the Pea Filling: ​Heat 1 teaspoon of oil in a pan over medium flame. ​Add the garlic cloves and green chilies. ​Add the fresh green peas and a pinch of salt. ​Sauté for 3 to 4 minutes until the raw smell disappears. Do not overcook them; they should just be soft enough to grind. ​Remove from heat and let the mixture cool completely. ​Once cooled, transfer to a grinder and pulse a few times to get a coarse, grainy texture. Avoid making a smooth paste. ​2. Make the Green Chutney: ​In a blender, combine coriander leaves, garlic, green chilies, lemon juice, roasted chana dal, salt, and a little water. ​Blend into a thick, spicy chutney. ​3. Assemble the Sandwich: ​Take two slices of bread. Apply a generous, thick layer of the coarse pea mixture on both slices. ​Place a cheese slice on top of the pea filling on one of the bread slices. This helps balance the spiciness of the peas and chutney. ​On two separate bread slices (the "top" slices), spread a layer of the spicy green chutney. ​Close the sandwiches by placing the chutney-spread bread over the cheese and pea-covered bread. ​4. Toast to Perfection: ​Heat a tawa (griddle) over low flame to ensure the sandwich gets extra crispy. ​Spread some butter on the tawa and place the sandwiches on it. ​Press gently and cook until the bottom is golden brown. ​Apply butter on the top side of the bread before flipping. ​Flip carefully and toast the other side for another 2 to 3 minutes until both sides are golden brown and the cheese inside has melted. ​5. Serving: ​Cut the sandwiches diagonally. * ​Serve hot with tomato ketchup and a side of potato chips for a cafe-style experience. 👍
